subject: Private Deployment payment schedule & SLA tradeoffs - Quantiva Health
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@quantiva.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@quantiva.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quantiva Private deployment commercial asks

Hi Marissa / David —

Great to meet on Tuesday. Quantiva is excited about the VPC/private deployment path. Before we get legal fully involved, procurement asked for a clear commercial example that addresses cashflow concerns. High level asks from our side: 

- Platform fee amortization (we'd like to avoid a single large upfront charge) — proposal: 60% upfront, 40% amortized over 12 months.
- Support tier: we need a strong first-90-day onboarding window (SRE retainer + faster P1 response).
- Discount: we are requesting a mid-market customer discount tiering given our 3-site deployment and 18-month expected run.

Can you share 1) an example payment schedule with a staggered platform fee; 2) what discounts are possible tied to our commit; and 3) any onboarding credits you can provide?

We’ve attached a short SOW outline to frame the scope.

Attachments: Quantiva_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF)

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Sr. Program Manager, Quantiva Health
sara@quantiva.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@quantiva.com>
Cc: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quantiva Private deployment commercial asks

Sara — thanks, this is helpful context. Writing up two pragmatic options that balance Quantiva’s cashflow preference and Redwood’s implementation risk. High level:

Option A — Accelerated amortization (preferred for lower total $):
- Platform fee: 15% discount if paid 100% upfront; otherwise 40% upfront + 60% amortized over 6 months.
- Onboarding: $75k SRE credit applied against first 3 months of retainer.
- SLA: standard enterprise SLA; 48-hour P1 during onboarding window.

Option B — Staggered with escrow and credits:
- Platform fee split: 25% upfront, 25% at go-live (30 days), remaining 50% amortized monthly over 9 months.
- Onboarding: 6 weeks of prioritized SRE hours plus $50k onboarding credit.
- Escrow: remaining amortized balance placed into a customer-held invoice escrow; if SLA breaches > 2 incidents in 90 days, 10% service credit applies against remaining balance.

I’ve attached a short commercial example and a straw-man SOW with the options called out. If you prefer, we can provide a blended example keyed to a committed 18-month term with a volume discount.

Next steps: which of the two options is closest to procurement’s appetite and would you want legal to start with a redline based on Option B?

Attachments: Marissa_Commercial_Examples.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Director — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quantiva Private deployment commercial asks — internal alignment

Team — forwarding Quantiva’s ask and the two options I proposed. Need quick alignment on acceptable exposure and how much onboarding credit we can commit without exec sign-off. Specifics:

- Risk profile: Quantiva is mid-market but multi-site (3 sites) and will need a private control plane + on-prem agent. Upfront effort for the first 60 days is non-trivial.
- Ask: can we go down to 25% upfront and amortize the remainder over 10 months? That gives them some cash relief and keeps our amortization reasonable.
- Onboarding credit: I proposed $50–75k in the email; prefer conservative $50k with the option to convert additional hours to time-and-materials.

David — thoughts on ops exposure and SLA concessions for first 90 days (we proposed 48-hour P1 in one option)?
Irene — pricing/legal: if procurement asks for escrow mechanics, what language do we need to protect recognition and prevent revenue leakage?

Thanks — need replies by EOD so I can circle back to Sara.

—Marissa
From: david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quantiva Private deployment commercial asks — internal alignment

Marissa — 2 quick points from ops:
1) 48-hour P1 is achievable for the first 60 days if we scope the SRE retainer explicitly (we'll need a hard cutover checklist and a go/no-go runbook). After that, revert to our standard P1 response time (72 hours SLA) unless they upgrade to the premium oncall tier.
2) 25% upfront plus 10-month amortization is reasonable on the finance side but leaves some collection risk if they default early — recommend we require a non-refundable 25% to cover initial engineering ramp and license escrow fees.

If legal is comfortable with escrow mechanics we can offer Option B-ish with 25% non-refundable and monthly amortization for the rest.

—David
From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@quantiva.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@quantiva.com>, procurement@quantiva.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Deployment payment schedule & SLA tradeoffs

Marissa — appreciate the options. Procurement/legal reviewed Option B and returned a redline with a counter-proposal. Key Quantiva counterpoints: 

- Payment schedule: 20% upfront, 40% over the first 6 months (quarterly), 40% at 12 months.
- Price protection: 90 days of protection from any price increases once we sign.
- SLA: we require a 48-hour P1 during onboarding and a guaranteed 2-week implementation window.

Attached is our redlined agreement and a cover note from procurement. Given our internal approvals, 20% upfront is their hard constraint. Can Redwood move to 20% or can you offer a trade (e.g., larger onboarding credit or reduced platform fee)?

Attachments: Quantiva_Redline_v2.docx (DOCX)

Thanks,
Tom Liu
CFO, Quantiva Health
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@quantiva.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@quantiva.com>, david_kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private Deployment payment schedule & SLA tradeoffs

Tom / Sara — thank you for the clear redline. We want to make this easy to get to signature while protecting our onboarding effort. Final commercial that I can approve without further exec sign-off: 

- Payment: 25% non-refundable upfront, 75% amortized monthly over 10 months (first amortization payment due 30 days after go-live).
- Onboarding credits: $50k applied against SRE retainer and first professional-services invoice (attached schedule).
- SLA: 48-hour P1 response during first 90 days with a defined go-live checklist; after 90 days, standard enterprise SLA (72-hour P1) unless customer purchases premium oncall.
- Price protection: 90 days from signature.

If Quantiva can accept 25% upfront, I’ll ask legal to generate the final order form with the amortization schedule and send a DocuSign link. If 25% is a showstopper, we can discuss increasing the onboarding credit to $80k in exchange for 25% being converted to 20% upfront and a 5% uplift on the monthly amortized payments (i.e., a small premium to compensate Redwood).

Next steps: please indicate acceptance of the 25% path or flag the credit + uplift counter by EOD PST and we’ll route the DocuSign.

Attachments: Marissa_Onboarding_Credit_Schedule.xlsx (XLSX)

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Director — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
